[TEST] BNP (or NT-proBNP) level.

[THOUGHT] Progressive exertional dyspnea with normal CBC, SpO2 at rest, ECG, CXR, and normal BNP makes primary cardiac failure, anemia, and obvious pulmonary consolidation unlikely. The key remaining possibilities are obstructive or interstitial lung disease, exercise-induced desaturation, or deconditioning; spirometry with lung volumes and DLCO will distinguish obstructive vs restrictive physiology and detect reduced gas transfer seen in ILD or pulmonary vascular disease. This single test will meaningfully narrow the diagnosis.

[TEST] Pulmonary function tests including spirometry with bronchodilator response, lung volumes, and DLCO.

Lung volumes: Normal

No peripheral edema, chest pain, cough, or immobilization history. The pattern (exertional symptoms only, normal resting studies) is most consistent with reduced exercise tolerance from physical deconditioning (poor cardiopulmonary fitness) rather than intrinsic cardiopulmonary disease.

[DIAGNOSIS] Deconditioning (reduced exercise tolerance/poor cardiopulmonary fitness).
